newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent closes near low on OPEC doubts.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent closes near low on OPEC doubts.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures closed near the lows in thin, skittish trade on Thursday after values soared then plummeted by 15 cents in a late U.S.-driven switchback ride, traders said.
Front month August Brent last traded at $17.85 a barrel, down 37 cents on the day and three cents off the low.
The slide was helped by bearish doubts about OPEC's ability to stem chronic overproduction and buoy sagging prices by abiding by long-ignored output quotas.

A spate of buying of U.S. crude futures by a major New York trader dragged August IPE to $18.04 from $17.84 shortly before the close. When the buying petered out, market-on-close selling took August careering back down to $17.85.
Brokers saw support for August at around $17.70 and the contract generally stuck in a range between $17.50 and $18.50.
In New York, August WTI was trading down 49 cents in new York at $19.03 a barrel at 1929 GMT. July gasoline was down 0.27 cent at 56.70 cents a gallon.
Bears took heart from an OPEC denial that Venezuela had admitted overproducing at the group's six-monthly talks in Vienna this week.
Brokers said any such admission would have been a constructive sign that members were facing reality and prepared to work to achieve a solution.
The denial implied face-saving for quota-busters was more important than price support, they said.
OPEC members currently pump out 2 million barrels per day above the agreed limit of 25.03 million bpd. OPEC oil ministers agreed on Thursday to freeze the figure for six months.
Front month July gas oil last traded at $161.75 a tonne, up $1.50 from Wednesday but only $1 off the day's low. The contract touched a high of $163.25 early on before crude trading began.
